record.original_question: Let m(4) be the minimum size of a family of 4-element subsets of a set S with the property that every 2-coloring of S makes at least one member of the family monochromatic. Determine m(4), or equivalently improve the known lower and upper bounds on m(4).

evidence.quote: Consider a family of 4-element subsets of a set S that has the property that any 2-coloring of S forces at least one of the 4-sets to be monochromatic. Let m(4) denote the minimal cardinality that such a family may have. ... Can you improve the lower or the upper bound?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A hypergraph H = (S, F), where F is a family of subsets of a set S, is said to have property B if there exists a 2-coloring of S (an assignment of one of two colors to each element of S) such that no member of F is monochromatic. For an integer n ≥ 2, let m(n) denote the minimum possible cardinality |F| of a family F of n-element subsets of a set S such that the hypergraph (S, F) does not have property B; equivalently, m(n) is the smallest number of n-element sets one must take so that, no matter how the underlying ground set is 2-colored, at least one of these n-sets is monochromatic.

Determine the exact value of m(4), or otherwise improve the best known lower and upper bounds on m(4).
artifact.status_search_result: The exact value m(4) = 23 was established by Östergård (2014) via exhaustive computer search, after the bounds had been narrowed to 21 ≤ m(4) ≤ 23. The corresponding question for m(5) and larger n remains open.

status_evidence.title: On the minimum size of 4-uniform hypergraphs without property B
status_evidence.snippet: Östergård established m(4) = 23 by exhaustive computer search.

status_evidence.title: Property B - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: m(2)=3, m(3)=7, m(4)=23; m(n) for n≥5 is unknown.
status_evidence.claim: The value m(4)=23 is established; higher cases open.
